title: Effect of genetic variation in the organic cation transporter 1 (OCT1) on metformin action
authors: Shu Y, Sheardown SA, Brown C, Owen RP, Zhang S, Castro RA, et al.
followUp: 180-minute oral glucose tolerance tests before and after metformin
population: Healthy volunteers genotyped for OCT1, 8 with reference alleles only and 12 with at least one reduced-function allele; with cellular assays, Oct1-knockout mice and mouse hepatocytes
funder: Supported by grants from the NIH (GM36780 and GM61390), core services of the General Clinical Research Center at San Francisco General Hospital (NIH MO1-RR00083-44) and the UCSF Liver Center (NIH P30 DK26743).
authorConflicts: The declared funding is public. Two of the twelve authors, S.A. Sheardown and L. Yue, are employees of GlaxoSmithKline, and a third GlaxoSmithKline scientist is thanked for advice and critical reading of the manuscript, so the record is classed industry for an industry role in the work and its publication.
result: Deletion of Oct1 in mouse hepatocytes reduced the effects of metformin on AMPK phosphorylation and gluconeogenesis, and in Oct1-deficient mice the glucose-lowering effect of metformin was abolished. Of 12 non-synonymous OCT1 polymorphisms, 7 showed reduced metformin uptake in transfected cells; among them 420del and R61C are common, with allele frequencies of 19% and 7.2% in people of European descent. In healthy volunteers, areas under the glucose concentration-time curve at baseline were 19,800 ± 1,480 against 19,800 ± 2,520 min/mg/dl for reference and variant carriers (P = 0.955), whereas after metformin the area was 18,200 ± 1,600 min/mg/dl in the 8 volunteers with reference alleles only and 21,300 ± 2,290 in the 12 carriers of a reduced-function allele (P = 0.004), with higher plasma glucose at most sampling points.
